title: Penguin Bill Length Analysis (R)
text:
The goal of this post is to showcase the varying bill lengths in millimeters for different penguin species by sex.


The data used in this post is sourced from the Palmer Penguins dataset shown below in Table 1.

Code
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)

head(penguins)




Table 1: Palmer Penguins Dataset



# A tibble: 6 × 8
  species island    bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm flipper_length_mm body_mass_g
  <fct>   <fct>              <dbl>         <dbl>             <int>       <int>
1 Adelie  Torgersen           39.1          18.7               181        3750
2 Adelie  Torgersen           39.5          17.4               186        3800
3 Adelie  Torgersen           40.3          18                 195        3250
4 Adelie  Torgersen           NA            NA                  NA          NA
5 Adelie  Torgersen           36.7          19.3               193        3450
6 Adelie  Torgersen           39.3          20.6               190        3650
# ℹ 2 more variables: sex <fct>, year <int>









The cleaned data can be found below in Table 2. To clean the data, records without a recorded sex were removed from the original dataset. The mean of the penguins’ bill length was then calculated after grouping by the penguins’ species and sex.

Code
modified_penguins <- penguins
modified_penguins <- drop_na(modified_penguins, sex)
modified_penguins <- modified_penguins |>
  group_by(species, sex) |>
  summarise(bill_length_mm = mean(bill_length_mm))

modified_penguins




Table 2: Bill length of penguins by species (Table).



# A tibble: 6 × 3
# Groups:   species [3]
  species   sex    bill_length_mm
  <fct>     <fct>           <dbl>
1 Adelie    female           37.3
2 Adelie    male             40.4
3 Chinstrap female           46.6
4 Chinstrap male             51.1
5 Gentoo    female           45.6
6 Gentoo    male             49.5







After cleaning the data and viewing the data it in Figure 1 below, it can be observed that male penguins on average across the listed species have longer bills compared to female penguins.


Code
modified_penguins_plot <- ggplot(data = modified_penguins, mapping = aes  (x = species,
    y = bill_length_mm,
    fill = sex)) +
    geom_col(position='dodge') +
    xlab("Species") +
    ylab("Bill Length (mm)") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 18))
modified_penguins_plot








Figure 1: Bill length of penguins by species (Chart).





Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

title: About
text:
Why Data Science
While getting my bachelor’s degree in computer science, I had the opportunity to write an undergraduate thesiswhich involved training a model to play Cassino, a lesser-known card game that my thesis mentor had played as a child. My research led me to learn about different machine learning methods that could train agents to play both deterministic and non-deterministic games. Although the model I trained to play Cassino performed very poorly, the knowledge and experience I gained from my thesis are what sparked my interest in data science.
